_comment: STARTER SKETCH — nothing reads this yet. Role/economics annotations for
the mons whose value the leaf eval structurally cannot price.
WHY A DATA FILE AND NOT AN LLM CALL. The knowledge here is ENUMERABLE (a
few dozen meta mons, each with a stable role), so it belongs in a
versioned, diffable artifact with zero inference latency — the same call
made for ps_sets_overrides.json, where a 40-line overlay fixed the
Kingambit Low Kick blindness that would otherwise have needed a model.
An LLM+RAG pass over the smogon corpus is a good way to DRAFT this file
(Phase 0 of the overlay plan) but the artifact is the deliverable, and it
must be human-reviewed before anything consumes it. Contextual judgements
that cannot be enumerated ('is THIS Kingambit worth holding on THIS board')
stay with the search or a later live overlay.
WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL. Three open items are each blocked on the same
missing fact — which mons are cleaners, which are resource anchors, which
are meant to lead:
1. Kingambit hold-back annuity: the eval now prices Supreme Overlord's
fallen-ally scaling (poke-engine c68f15a) but still cannot see the
OPPORTUNITY COST of spending the cleaner early; it needs to know the
mon is a cleaner at all.
2. Weather preservation: measured 43% rain uptime with 41% of Swift Swim
moves clicked OUTSIDE rain — the search does not treat the setter's
survival as a resource, or the weather clock as a wasting asset.
3. Canonical-lead weighting: the preview matrix is nearly flat (row-min
spreads 0.01-0.12 at any depth) so lead choice is close to a coin
flip among near-ties; paste slot-1 and role are real human priors.
SAFETY CONTRACT: every consumer must degrade to current behaviour on a
missing entry. This file may only ADD information; it must never be
required. Absent species = today's engine, unchanged.
SCHEMA (per normalized species; `ability` qualifies when the role depends
on it, since the same species with another ability is a different mon):
tags         role labels, the primary key for consumers
`disruptor` is its own role, distinct from wall and attacker:
a mon whose job is to deny the opponent's turn rather than to
absorb or threaten damage — forcing switches (Whirlwind, Red
Card), locking a move (Encore), shutting off status and setup
(Taunt), or punishing an attack directly (Mirror Coat). It is
easy to mistake for a lead because it wants to act early, but
it is not trying to win the first turn — it is trying to make
the opponent's turn worthless, which is why leading it is a
CHOICE rather than its definition.
ability      role holds only for this ability (omit = any)
value_curve  how worth changes over a game: flat | grows_with_own_faints
| decays_with_weather_clock | grows_with_hazards
preserve     how badly losing it costs beyond its own HP: low|med|high
resource     field state this mon CREATES; its death ends it
requires     field state this mon NEEDS to be worth its slot
entry_condition  precondition for this mon's PLAN, not its survival: e.g.
full_hp when a Sash/Multiscale sequence needs a clean
entry. Distinct from preserve (cost of losing it) and
requires (a field state). Added 2026-07-31 after the
Ceruledge entry needed a concept neither field had.
first_entry_boost marks a one-shot entry resource: Booster
Energy is consumed the first time the mon comes in and never
returns, so a Booster set is a different Pokemon on its second
switch-in than its first. WHEN it is spent is a real decision
the leaf eval does not price.
An entry condition is not only LOST — it can be MANUFACTURED
and even RESTORED, which the field alone does not say. The
avenues, cheapest first: (1) entry after a faint, which is a
free switch that takes no hit; (2) a SLOW PIVOT — Chilly
Reception, or U-turn/Volt Switch/Flip Turn from something
slower — which brings the mon in without it taking that turn's
attack, strictly safer than a hard switch; (3) HEALING WISH,
which restores a teammate to full HP and so RE-ENABLES a
full_hp condition outright; (4) Wish passing, partially;
(5) hazard removal or Boots, which protect the entry rather
than create it. Measured over 490 games: of our full_hp mons
that went on to set up, 58% came in on a HARD SWITCH (the
riskiest route), 25% off a faint, and only 6% off a slow pivot.
entry_enablers  teammates or moves that manufacture or restore this mon's
entry condition. Recorded because it is a TEAM property the
per-species fields cannot express, and because it turns a
constraint into something actionable: a Healing Wish user on
the same side means the condition is recoverable, not spent.
lead_intent  human intent to lead it: avoid | neutral | strong
conditional   list of {when, ...overrides}: role/value that only exists
`when` vocabulary is of TWO kinds and they are not
interchangeable: TEAM-COMPOSITION (opponent_has:<tag>,
opponent_lacks:<tag>) is knowable at team preview, while
BOARD-STATE (board:hazards_up, board:weather_up) is only true
at some moments of a game. Spinblocking is the type case: the
Ghost typing blocks Rapid Spin ALWAYS, but it is worth nothing
until hazards are actually standing that the other side wants
to clear — so the tag is unconditional and the VALUE is
board-gated.
axis          which side of the split a role operates on — {attacks: ...}
and, for anything tagged wall, {defends: ...}. Values:
physical | special | mixed. A wall is only a wall against one
side, and a sweeper only threatens through one stat, so a bare
'wall' or 'setup-sweeper' tag leaves out the thing that decides
whether it checks the mon in front of it. Set per-set where a
species splits: Kyurem's Choice Specs set attacks specially
`defends` belongs on anything that WALLS — it is the field that
says what the mon actually checks, and a bare 'wall' tag without
it is close to useless. It does NOT belong on an offensive pivot,
which switches for momentum rather than to absorb a side. Read it
off the EV spread: Slowking-Galar's 252 HP / 252 SpD spreads make
it a SPECIAL wall on both its sets, while Corviknight's Impish
248 / 252 Def makes it a physical one.
`attacks` belongs on ATTACKERS. A genuinely utility set — a
weather setter, a screens lead, a Wish passer — carrying one
weak attack does not have a meaningful offensive axis, and
listing one implies a threat it does not pose. Omit it unless a
tag actually claims an offensive role.

sets          for species that genuinely split into different Pokemon
Each set may carry `prevalence`: roughly what fraction of that
species' sets run it, estimated as the signature move's usage
divided by 25% (a set holds four moves, so any one move tops
Three signature kinds, in order of preference: a MOVE unique to
the set (usage / 25%), else the ITEM (usage directly — one item
Ability is often ORTHOGONAL to the set rather than a set of its
own — a Choice Specs Dragapult may run either Infiltrator or
Clear Body — so an ability split is recorded at species level in
Signatures are NOT always one-dimensional. A set can be defined
by a COMBINATION — a particular move with a particular item, or
move+item+ability together — and two sets may share a move while
differing on item, or share an item while differing on ability.
Where a single signature cannot separate them, say so in the set
fact rather than forcing one dimension to carry the split.
`ability_split` and mentioned in the fact, not modelled as a
A set defined by the ABSENCE of a signature must use the
residual, never a proxy: Dragonite's non-Dragon-Dance build
runs Roost, but so do Dragon Dance sets, so counting Roost
double-counts and the two shares summed over 100%.
SET SHARES DO NOT PARTITION and should not be forced to 100%.
The named sets are overlapping ARCHETYPES, not exclusive
categories — a Booster Energy Iron Valiant can be both the
'Calm Mind' and the 'Mixed' build, so shares can legitimately
sum over 100 where archetypes overlap and under 100 where the
write-ups skip a common build. Where named sets cover under
80%, an explicit 'Other / unnamed' entry carries the remainder
so a reader can see the uncovered space instead of assuming
the list is exhaustive. Raging Bolt was the warning case: its
two named sets covered 16% while the real majority build
(Booster Energy, 52%) went unnamed by the analysis.
Some sets have NO positive signature — an all-out-attacker build
is defined by what it lacks, and a form item like Wellspring Mask
is on every set. Those get a RESIDUAL estimate (whatever the
signature-derived sets leave over) with prevalence_method set to
'residual' so a reader can weight it accordingly: it absorbs the
combined error of the others and assumes the sets partition
cleanly. An estimate beats a blank — but label how it was made.

EVERY set (typing, ability); each entry here carries what is
true only of that one. A consumer should key off the inferred
set when it has one and fall back to the species otherwise.
against certain opposing teams. Static fields describe the
DEFAULT case; a matching `when` replaces them. Added
2026-07-31 — Magic Bounce Hatterene is a hazard-denial
anchor against a team with setters and close to dead weight
against one without, and a single `preserve` cannot say
both. `when` vocabulary: opponent_has:<tag>, opponent_lacks:<tag>.
deployment    HOW the mon is meant to be brought in, which the search
cannot infer from the board: lead | bait-switch | pivot-cycle
| late-cleaner | sacrifice. Distinct from lead_intent (which
only answers 'should it start the game'). bait-switch means
it is sent in to INVITE a specific opponent action and punish
it — Hatterene switching in on a predicted hazard turn to
bounce it is the type case, and it is explicitly NOT a lead.
Values: lead | bait-switch | pivot-cycle | late-cleaner |
sacrifice | setup-window (needs a FREE entry to begin a
multi-turn plan — Ceruledge and Multiscale Dragonite).
sequence      the ordered play a mon's value actually comes from, for the
cases where no single turn of it looks good. Added 2026-07-31
(user): Ceruledge's line deliberately TAKES a hit, so a search
scoring each turn on immediate safety declines the whole plan.
This is the beyond-horizon knowledge in its most explicit form
— write the chain down rather than hoping depth finds it.
fact          WHAT THE MON DOES, plainly. This is the only field a consumer
WHERE THE META IS GENUINELY SPREAD, SAY SO. Do not manufacture
a modal answer: Darkrai's items run Boots 21% / Specs 18% /
Scarf 16% / Life Orb 12% / Leftovers 11%, so 'usually Choice
Scarf' is a confident claim the data does not support. A
confidently wrong belief is worse than an honestly vague one —
the same lesson the opponent-belief work learned the hard way,
where sharper-but-wrong sets lost to calibrated spread. Prefer
'runs several sets' plus the `sets` list over inventing a
single answer.
should ever be shown: present tense, mechanically true, and
OPPONENT-AGNOSTIC. No campaign history, no commit hashes, no
named opponents — a note about how one specific ladder bot
builds its teams is per-opponent knowledge that belongs in the
scouting book, and feeding it here would mislead us against
everyone else. Narrative prose also invites a downstream model
to narrativise; plain facts do not.
provenance    HUMAN REVIEW ONLY, never shown to a consumer: where the claim
came from, what corrected what, citations and commits. Kept so
a reviewer can audit a fact without that history contaminating
the fact itself.
REVIEW RULE: an entry without `evidence` is a guess and should not ship.
Role tags are TESTABLE against behaviour — the Kingambit timing analysis
(first-entry turn, allies fallen at entry) is the template; a claimed
'cleaner' whose deployment timing does not move after wiring is a claim
that failed, not a fact.

kingambit.fact: Supreme Overlord raises its power by 10% for each fallen ally, so it is weakest at full team and strongest last. Sucker Punch gives it priority. Spending it early forfeits the scaling it exists for.
kingambit.provenance: Supreme Overlord = +10% power per fallen ally (abilities.rs:2257), now mirrored into threat_vs (c68f15a). Timing instrument: we first deploy it ~T9 with 0.44 allies down and 77% of the time with ZERO down, vs the ladder population's T13.0 / 0.96. fp is equally guilty, so this is absolute strength, not fp-gap.
kingambit.single_build_note: Item choice varies (Leftovers 45%, Black Glasses 23%, Air Balloon 11%) but the Swords Dance role does not change with it.

pelipper.fact: Drizzle sets rain the moment it enters, and Damp Rock extends the duration. The rain ends early if another weather setter replaces it.
pelipper.provenance: rain_audit over 27 rain-team games: 43% average uptime where a piloted Damp Rock team lives 60-80%; uptime tracked outcomes (50% in wins vs 40% in losses). Rain teams benched at 29.2% board-only, the only below-pool-CI archetype.
pelipper.single_build_note: One build: Damp Rock on 85% of sets.

barraskewda.fact: Swift Swim doubles its Speed in rain, so it outspeeds most of the field only while rain is up and is ordinary without it.
barraskewda.provenance: 41% of Swift Swim moves across those games were clicked OUTSIDE rain (60 in / 42 out) — the search spends the abuser while its enabling condition is down.
barraskewda.single_build_note: One build: Choice Band on 86% of sets.

torkoal.fact: Drought sets sun on entry and Heat Rock extends it. Its own Speed is very low, so it exists to enable partners.
torkoal.provenance: same audit: sun leaks identically (43% uptime) but sun teams win anyway (63%) because Protosynthesis abusers fall back on Booster Energy — so preserve pressure is genuinely LOWER here than for rain. Recorded to stop a future fix over-generalising 'weather setter' into one rule.
torkoal.single_build_note: One build: Heat Rock on 82% of sets.

glimmora.fact: Toxic Debris sets Toxic Spikes when it is hit by a physical move. Stealth Rock and Mortal Spin give it hazard control, and Focus Sash guarantees it gets at least one layer down.
glimmora.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Glimmora (gen9ou) — Lead]: the Lead set exists to deny setup — it stops "Ting-Lu from setting up entry hazards multiple times and Hatterene from trying to deny Stealth Rock with Magic Bounce". Confirms the suicide-lead role: its job is completed on the turns it survives, not by surviving. Directly relevant to richwoman, whose hazard stack is anchored by Ting-Lu (45 leads).

grimmsnarl.fact: Prankster gives its status moves priority, so it sets Reflect and Light Screen before being attacked. Light Clay extends both to eight turns.
grimmsnarl.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Grimmsnarl (gen9ou) — Dual Screens]: recommended set is Reflect / Light Screen / Taunt / Spirit Break with LIGHT CLAY, an item bought purely to extend the side conditions it leaves behind — the definition of expendable team-persistent support. Matches the monotype screens-setter precedent.
grimmsnarl.single_build_note: One build: Light Clay on 85% of sets.

slowkinggalar.fact: Regenerator restores a third of its HP whenever it switches out, so repeated entries cost it almost nothing. Chilly Reception switches it out while setting snow, and Future Sight lands two turns later so it threatens even after leaving the field.
slowkinggalar.provenance: Regenerator pivots are net-positive on entry (fp routes hazard cycles through them: pays 12.5%, regains 33%) — the hazard_cycle finding. Also the mon whose speed floor produced the false Choice Scarf call (88f1f17), so its canonical spread is bulky with ~0 Speed. [Trimmed 2026-07-31: the fact had noted its low Speed investment, which was only interesting because of a speed-inference bug on our side — session detail, not a property a reader needs. Removed.]

gholdengo.fact: Good as Gold makes it immune to status moves. Its Ghost typing blocks Rapid Spin, so hazards its side has set cannot be spun away while it is alive — this is true of every set, being a property of its typing rather than its moves. Air Balloon, its most common item, adds a temporary Ground immunity.
gholdengo.provenance: USER-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: my entry reduced a top-3 usage Pokemon to 'spinblocker', omitting that it is a primary win condition. Usage data confirms the correction — Shadow Ball 21.1% and Make It Rain 20.8% are its two most-used moves, Nasty Plot 12.8%, Recover 12.5%, Trick 8.4% (Choice Scarf is 33% of its items), Thunder Wave 4.1% with Hex 3.1%, Air Balloon 44% of items. Smogon's analysis calls it "both a defensive and offensive glue on virtually any team" and carries a dedicated Offensive Nasty Plot set. SCHEMA LIMITATION this exposed: the file annotates a SPECIES, but this mon has several sets with genuinely different roles (Nasty Plot sweeper, Choice Scarf Trick, defensive status/Hex). Tags and fact now cover all of them, which is lossy — a consumer cannot tell WHICH set is in front of it. The set-inference tiers already identify that at runtime, so a future consumer should key role off the inferred set rather than the species alone. Same class of gap as the sole-remover team-property problem. [Refined 2026-07-31 (user): spinblocking is a TYPING property so the tag is unconditional — what is conditional is whether it matters, which needs hazards actually on the field, not merely a hazard-setter on the roster. Split into per-set entries at the same time.]

gliscor.fact: Poison Heal turns being poisoned into recurring healing rather than damage, so it has to be statused before it does anything — the Toxic Orb it carries applies that poison at the end of a turn. Protect does two jobs: it blocks Knock Off, which matters because losing the orb disables Poison Heal outright, and it stalls turns while the healing ticks. Substitute blocks status and chip from behind.
gliscor.provenance: The flagship annuity case. Stall audit: fp's Poison Heal Gliscor played its FULL PP budget and generated 22.8 mons of free healing over three marathons while ours clicked 6 moves in ~711 turns. Eval terms shipped for exactly this (poke-engine 76af1e9: POISON_HEAL_STATUSED 15->35, PENDING +15) and our Gliscor now SubToxes at full budget. Known race: the naked orb walked into Knock Off on entry in 2/3 marathons, so activation timing is itself the play. [USER-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: the fact described Protect as only stalling for heal ticks. Its other job is blocking Knock Off to keep the Toxic Orb, without which the whole set does nothing.]
gliscor.single_build_note: One build: Toxic Orb on 99% of sets — Poison Heal requires it.

conditional.note: Hazard removal is only worth something while the opponent is setting hazards. Against a team that sets none, the removal move is a wasted slot.

greattusk.fact: Rapid Spin removes entry hazards for the whole team. Protosynthesis raises its Speed, letting it outpace threats that would normally be faster. Its removal is a service to teammates, not a personal benefit. Booster Energy is consumed on its FIRST entry and does not come back, so the stat boost exists for that one switch-in only — after it, the same Pokemon is unboosted unless its weather or terrain is up.
greattusk.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Great Tusk (gen9ou) — Offensive Utility / Defensive]: "Rapid Spin allows it to remove entry hazards for its teammates, and the Speed boost lets it scare out usually faster threats like Darkrai and Iron Crown"; also "a staple on Sticky Web teams". SOLE-REMOVER CAVEAT: preserve:high holds only when it is the team's only remover — a TEAM property this per-species file cannot express (schema gap). Hazard chip is our pinned loss mechanism (SR = 21% of damage taken), so the remover is a team-persistent resource. [SCHEMA GAP, reviewer note: preserve also depends on whether OUR OWN team carries another remover — a team property this per-species file cannot express, and `conditional` only covers opponent facts. Moved out of the consumer-facing note 2026-07-31.]

dragonite.fact: Multiscale halves incoming damage only at full HP, so it needs an undamaged entry to function. Roost restores that condition. Dragon Dance turns one safe turn into a sweep. Most sets tera Normal, which gives Extreme Speed same-type damage and turns its priority move into a finisher.
dragonite.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Dragonite (gen9ou)]: Roost-based sets "give Dragonite easy setup opportunities" and let it check Ogerpon-W, Iron Moth and Rillaboom, "with Multiscale intact". Same entry_condition family as Ceruledge: Multiscale only halves damage at FULL HP, so entry chip deletes the defensive half of the wincon before it sets up — which is why the standard set runs Boots. The eval prices Multiscale when at full HP but cannot price PRESERVING full HP for a later sweep. [USER-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: the sequence omitted terastallizing. Usage confirms Tera Normal on 57% of sets, far ahead of Flying 16%, and Extreme Speed is its third-most-used move at 18% — the tera exists to give that priority move STAB.]
sequence: enter at FULL HP — Multiscale halves the incoming hit only from full, and Heavy-Duty Boots are what keep it full through hazards
Dragon Dance while Multiscale absorbs the first attack, raising Attack and Speed
sweep with Earthquake and its coverage move
Terastallize to Normal when the sweep needs finishing: it gives Extreme Speed same-type damage on top of the Dragon Dance boost, and priority ignores Speed entirely
Roost when the sweep stalls instead: it restores full HP and with it Multiscale, buying another setup turn
dragonite.sequence_note: Two ways to close, and they compete for the same turns. Tera Normal converts Extreme Speed into the finisher, beating anything faster or already weakened regardless of Speed; Roost instead refreshes Multiscale for a second setup window. Chip damage that prevents reaching full HP removes the Roost option permanently, which pushes it toward the tera line.

ceruledge.fact: Weak Armor raises its Speed when it is hit. Bitter Blade heals it for half the damage dealt. Focus Sash survives one hit but only from full HP. Shadow Sneak provides priority. Psychic Noise blocking recovery also matters in the long grinds where the recovery war is even.
